Alternative, the pipette volume displacement could be used to cause some kind of suction to get it to grip.

Panel C was rebuilt entirely in c2ff12a as part of the longitudinal-pivot / sideways-tilt geometry change — the two arms now grip the trough's two **short end caps** and the pivot pin runs along the long axis L through both end caps, so they're symmetric on opposite ends rather than both on one side. Same correction is consistent across panels A–D and the new pin-slot Panel E (5d59dd0).

The dip-vs-scoop concern was folded in as part of the geometry rework in c2ff12a: the baseline motion is now a **J-curve plunge** — the trough enters Z↓ then immediately translates a few mm in X while continuing down, i.e. "put it down then drag it" rather than a pure vertical dip — followed by a Z↑ that drags the rim under a fixed bed-edge **strike-off bar** (now baseline-required, not optional) which is the closest-to-bimodal trick available without adding a second axis on the bucket. The bimodal / OT-2-tip-eject / pipette-suction ideas are noted as "active variations to prototype" in `docs/manuscript/main.tex` §"Design variations"; they all require an actuator on the bucket and so trade off against the gantry-only / no-second-axis constraint, which I'm now hardening into the parametric CAD DFM check (see follow-up commit).

`render_static()` assumes there are at least two stable wells and will raise `IndexError` when `result.stable_wells` is empty or has only one entry (e.g., if parameters are tweaked and the design becomes mono-stable). Consider handling the non-bimodal case explicitly (raise a clear `ValueError` with `result.summary()`, or fall back to a single-pose rendering) so the script fails with an actionable message instead of a crash.

`_snap_trajectory()` also indexes `wells[0]`/`wells[-1]` and will crash for mono-stable / non-bimodal results. It would be more robust to validate `len(result.stable_wells) >= 2` up front and raise a clear error (or return a degenerate trajectory) so `render_animation()` can handle non-bimodal parameter sets gracefully.

`test_lhs_is_reproducible_under_seed` compares floating-point lists for exact equality. Even with a fixed seed this can be brittle across NumPy/SciPy versions and platforms (minor FP differences), especially since `requirements.txt` only sets minimum versions. Prefer `pytest.approx`/`np.allclose` (or compare the raw LHS unit-cube samples) so the test still catches nondeterminism without becoming flaky.

`render_violin()` zips in `scale` from `INPUT_SCALE` but never uses it. This is easy to miss and can confuse future edits (it looks like an intended unit conversion). Either apply `scale` to `x` before bucketing/labeling, or drop it from the loop to avoid dead variables.
```suggestion
        for ax, key, label in zip(axes, INPUT_KEYS, INPUT_LABELS):
```

`run_sweep()` is documented to silently skip diverged/non-converged points, but this integration test requires `len(results) == 9`. If CalculiX drops even one point (e.g., due to solver variability on different runners), this will fail despite the intended “best-effort” behavior. Either make `run_sweep()` strict in test mode (raise if any point fails), or relax the assertion (e.g., require a minimum count and coverage of both wells).

The `article` class doesn't support an `8.5pt` option (standard sizes are 10/11/12pt), so this will be reported as an unused global option and the document will compile at the default font size instead of 8.5pt. Consider switching to a class that supports smaller base sizes (or explicitly setting the base font size) so the output matches the intended RSC styling.

`\usepackage{sectsty}` will look for `sectsty.sty`, but the repo vendors `paper/secsty.sty` (missing the "t") even though it declares `\ProvidesPackage{sectsty}`. ```


_embed_context() wraps each file in a triple-backtick fence, but several embedded files (e.g. README.md) contain their own ``` fences. That will prematurely terminate the fence and corrupt the prompt payload sent to Edison. Consider using a longer fence (e.g. 4+ backticks chosen based on the max run in the content), or switch to an escaping strategy / indentation-based quoting, and read files with an explicit encoding to avoid locale-dependent failures.

`os.path.getsize(out)` is called unconditionally; if `model.Write()` returns false (or partially fails) this will raise `FileNotFoundError` and obscure the real failure. Gate the size lookup and the subsequent read/roundtrip on `ok` (or check `Path(out).exists()`), and print a clear failure message when write fails.
```suggestion
out_path = pathlib.Path(out)
if ok and out_path.exists():
    print(f"Wrote {out}: ok={ok}, size={os.path.getsize(out)} bytes")

    m2 = r3.File3dm.Read(out)
    print(f"Re-read ok, objects={len(m2.Objects)}")
    for obj in m2.Objects:
        g = obj.Geometry
        try:
            bbox = g.GetBoundingBox()
            print(f"  - {type(g).__name__:14s}  bbox min={bbox.Min}  max={bbox.Max}")
        except Exception:
            print(f"  - {type(g).__name__}")
else:
    print(f"Failed to write {out}: ok={ok}")
```

`render_spin()` opens each PNG frame with `Image.open(png)` but never closes the underlying file handle. On some platforms (notably Windows), this can prevent `TemporaryDirectory()` cleanup and cause flaky runs. Use a context manager (or explicitly close) and store a fully in-memory image (e.g., convert + copy) in `frames`.
```suggestion
            with Image.open(png) as frame:
                frames.append(
                    frame.convert("P", palette=Image.ADAPTIVE).copy()
                )
```

`--frames` and `--fps` accept any integer, but `frames=0` will raise `IndexError` at `frames[0].save(...)` and `fps=0` will cause a division-by-zero in `duration=int(1000 / fps)`. Validate these args (and optionally width/height) and return a clear error message before rendering.
